stories.headline: US payrolls unexpectedly fall 23,000 in July; May-June revised down by 103,000

key_facts.fact: Total US nonfarm payroll employment declined by 23,000 in July 2026, while the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Aug. 7.
key_facts.excerpt: Both nonfarm payroll employment (-23,000) and the unemployment rate (4.1 percent) changed little in July, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.

key_facts.fact: Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast an 80,000 gain in July payrolls and an unchanged 4.2% jobless rate.
key_facts.excerpt: Nonfarm payrolls forecast to increase 80,000 in July; Unemployment rate expected to hold steady at 4.2%

key_facts.fact: Revisions cut a combined 103,000 jobs from the May and June reports, leaving average monthly job growth over the past year at just 34,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Revisions shaved a combined 103,000 jobs from the May and June reports, meaning the US has added an average of just 34,000 jobs per month over the past year.

key_facts.fact: Employment fell in local government education (-50,000), retail trade (-19,000) and financial activities (-14,000), while health care added 22,000 jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: In July, employment in local government education declined by 50K and retail trade decreased by 19K... Employment also declined in financial activities (-14K)... In contrast, the health care sector added 22K jobs.

key_facts.fact: Average hourly earnings rose 3.2% year over year to $37.62 and the labor force participation rate was 61.4%.
key_facts.excerpt: Average hourly earnings increased 3.2% over the year, with the labour force participation rate stable at 61.4%.

key_facts.fact: Two days earlier, ADP reported private employers added only 44,000 jobs in July, down from 95,000 in June and below the 75,000 consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: Private companies added 44,000 jobs in July, a slowdown from the 95,000 the prior month and below market expectations, ADP reported Wednesday.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign Mecca pact: an attack on one is an attack on all

key_facts.fact: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the trilateral joint defence agreement in Mecca on Friday, Aug. 7, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan today signed a new joint defense agreement, creating a NATO-style collective defense alliance... signed by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Pakistani Prime Minister Muhammad Sharif at the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence.

key_facts.fact: The joint statement says the pact 'stipulates that an armed attack carried out against any one of the three states shall be considered an attack against all of them.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The Agreement aims to bolster collective deterrence against all forms of aggression and stipulates that an armed attack carried out against any one of the three states shall be considered an attack against all of them," the joint statement said.

key_facts.fact: A Turkish official said the agreement is purely defensive, is not aimed at any specific actor, is open to other regional countries and does not replace existing bilateral or multilateral arrangements.
key_facts.excerpt: "The pact includes a collective defence clause. It is purely defensive in nature, pledging mutual support only for defence," a Turkish official said.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows nearly a year of negotiations and comes after Iran and its allies began firing on Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states and blockading their energy shipments, since the US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan will sign a joint defence agreement in Mecca on Friday... amid regional turmoil with Gulf states coming under fire from Iran after it was attacked by the U.S. and Israel. ... Agreement follows nearly a year of negotiations.

key_facts.fact: Turkey has NATO's second-largest military, Saudi Arabia is the Arab world's leading military and economic power, and Pakistan is the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Pakistan has deployed about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to the kingdom.
key_facts.excerpt: Turkey has NATO's second-largest military. Saudi Arabia, the strongest Gulf state... while Pakistan is the only nuclear-armed Muslim country... Pakistan has since deployed about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to the kingdom.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said on X that the agreement establishes a framework for a long-term defense partnership strengthening deterrence, coordination and integration among the three countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Khalid bin Salman stated that the agreement, signed in Makkah, "establishes a framework for a long-term defense partnership between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, strengthening deterrence, coordination, and integration among our brotherly nations."

stories.headline: Iran's draft Hormuz plan would bar US and Israeli ships and charge tolls; oil jumps 4%

key_facts.fact: Iranian state media reported on Aug. 6 that Iran's parliament is reviewing a plan to ban ships linked to the US, Israel and other 'hostile countries' from transiting the Strait of Hormuz until Tehran is compensated for war damage.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's parliament is reviewing a plan to ban ships linked to the U.S., Israel and other "hostile countries" from transiting the Strait of Hormuz until Tehran is compensated for war damage, according to Iranian state media.

key_facts.fact: The draft would impose fees of up to 7% of cargo value on commercial vessels transiting the strait and fine violators up to 20% of cargo value.
key_facts.excerpt: The plan would impose fees of up to 7% of cargo value on commercial vessels that pass through the strait. It would also fine ships 20% of cargo if they violate Iran's conditions.

key_facts.fact: A US official told NPR that any temporary routes would be 'without any impediments — meaning no approvals or permissions and no tolls or charges,' calling Hormuz an international waterway no party controls.
key_facts.excerpt: "Any temporary routes will be without any impediments — meaning no approvals or permissions and no tolls or charges. The Strait of Hormuz is an international waterway and no party controls the lanes or the ability to transit through them," a U.S. official told NPR.

key_facts.fact: Oil futures rose about 3-4% on the reports: WTI for September settled up $2.07 (2.75%) at $77.29 a barrel and October Brent closed up $3.04 (3.8%) at $82.49.
key_facts.excerpt: NYMEX WTI crude for September delivery settled up $2.07, or 2.75%, at $77.29 bbl. ICE Brent crude for October closed up $3.04, or 3.8%, at $82.49 bbl.

key_facts.fact: The reported terms landed days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and President Donald Trump said a deal to reopen the waterway could be announced before the end of the week.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's plans for the Hormuz were unveiled days after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and President Donald Trump said a deal to unlock the waterway could be announced before the end of this week.

key_facts.fact: Iran said on Aug. 5 it was finalizing an agreement with Oman under which ships would enter through a northern corridor near the Iranian coast and exit through a southern corridor near the Omani coast; the strait has been effectively shut since the war began on Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran on Wednesday said it was finalizing an agreement on shipping routes with Oman... ships would enter through the strait's northern corridor near the Iranian coast and exit through the southern corridor near the Omani coast.

stories.headline: Trump sets 15% tariff and import price floors on polysilicon to counter China

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump signed a Section 232 proclamation on Aug. 6, 2026 imposing a minimum import price program and a 15% ad valorem tariff on polysilicon derivatives.
key_facts.excerpt: I determine that it is necessary and appropriate to impose a 15 percent ad valorem rate of duty on imports of polysilicon derivatives... IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this sixth day of August, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six.

key_facts.fact: The minimum import prices are $21 per kilogram for polysilicon, $100 per kilogram for ingots and wafers, $0.22 per watt for solar cells and $0.38 per watt for solar modules.
key_facts.excerpt: (i) $21 per kilogram for polysilicon; (ii) $100 per kilogram for polysilicon ingots and wafers; (iii) $0.22 per watt for solar cells; and (iv) $0.38 per watt for solar modules.

key_facts.fact: The measures take effect on Dec. 4, 2026, 120 days after signing.
key_facts.excerpt: The remedies will take effect 120 days after signing.

key_facts.fact: Polysilicon is the raw material used in semiconductors and solar panels and is primarily produced by China; the action is aimed at supporting domestic chip and solar supply chains needed to compete with Beijing on artificial intelligence and energy.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House on Thursday imposed a series of price floors and a 15% tariff on products made from polysilicon, the raw material used in semiconductors and solar panels that is primarily produced by China.

key_facts.fact: For Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and EU members the combined duty is capped at 15%, while UK products face 10%; the new tariff replaces a narrower solar cell and module safeguard that expired in February 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: For products of the United Kingdom subject to tariffs under this proclamation, the applicable rate of duty... shall be 10 percent... They will also replace a similar but narrower safeguard tariff on solar cells and modules that I imposed in my first term, and which expired in February 2026.

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced the order in the Oval Office; companies that begin construction of US polysilicon, ingot, wafer or cell plants before the end of Trump's term can qualify for tariff exemptions under an onshoring program.
key_facts.excerpt: The executive order will help boost the U.S. supply chain, Secretary Howard Lutnick said in the Oval Office.

stories.headline: FDA approves Replimune's melanoma immunotherapy Tudriqev after two rejections

key_facts.fact: The FDA on Aug. 6, 2026 granted accelerated approval to Replimune's Tudriqev (vusolimogene oderparepvec), formerly RP1, in combination with Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo for advanced melanoma that progressed after anti-PD-1 therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The Food and Drug Administration on Thursday approved a Replimune treatment for advanced melanoma, ending a saga that saw the medicine rejected twice before physicians, patients and agency advisers persuaded the regulator to reconsider.

key_facts.fact: Tudriqev is an engineered oncolytic virus injected directly into tumors, where it replicates and destroys cancer cells that then release immune-stimulating proteins.
key_facts.excerpt: An engineered oncolytic virus, Tudriqev is injected directly into tumors, where it reproduces and destroys diseased cells which then release immune-stimulating proteins.

key_facts.fact: In the 140-patient Phase 1/2 IGNYTE trial the Tudriqev-Opdivo combination produced an objective response rate of 24.2% with a median duration of response of 14.1 months.
key_facts.excerpt: In the IGNYTE trial, which comprised 140 patients, Tudriqev plus Opdivo elicited an objective response rate of 24.2%, with a median duration of response of 14.1 months.

key_facts.fact: FDA reviewers had argued in briefing documents that the trial data were 'not interpretable,' but the agency's Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted 10-3 in the drug's favor the week before.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, the FDA's Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee (CTGTAC), voted 10-3 in support of the drug... FDA reviewers said data from Replimune's registrational trial were "not interpretable."

key_facts.fact: The therapy was rejected in July 2025 and again in April 2026; continued approval depends on an ongoing Phase 3 trial expected to read out in late 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA granted Tudriqev an "accelerated" approval, meaning continued licensure is contingent on the success of an ongoing Phase 3 trial... expected to produce results in late 2027.

key_facts.fact: Leerink Partners analyst Daina Graybosch projected peak annual sales of $618 million for the drug, while Wall Street consensus is closer to $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Leerink Partners analyst Daina Graybosch predicted the drug could achieve $618 million in peak annual sales if approved, while Wall Street's consensus is closer to $1 billion.

stories.headline: Ukraine hits two more Russian refineries as Russia says it downed 605 drones overnight

key_facts.fact: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Thursday, Aug. 6 that Ukraine's military struck two oil refineries deep inside Russia — Bashneft-Novoil in Bashkortostan and Slavneft-Yanos in the Yaroslavl region — saying the strikes were 'strengthening the prospects for diplomacy.'
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the military hit two oil refineries deep inside Russia, the Bashneft-Novoil refinery in the republic of Bashkortostan and the Slavnet-Yanos refinery in the Yaroslavl region. He said the strikes were "strengthening the prospects for diplomacy."

key_facts.fact: Yaroslavl regional governor Mikhail Evrayev said the refinery caught fire after debris struck its storage tanks and called it the region's 'most massive' drone attack of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Mikhail Evrayev, the regional governor in Russia's Yaroslavl region, said the oil refinery was on fire... He later called it the region's "most massive" drone attack of the war.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Ministry of Defence said its air defences intercepted and destroyed 605 Ukrainian drones overnight over Russian territory and annexed Crimea.
key_facts.excerpt: "During the night … air defence systems intercepted and destroyed 605 Ukrainian aerial drones," the ministry said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: Russian strikes overnight killed at least six people in Ukraine — three in Balakliya in the Kharkiv region and three in the northern Sumy region, where at least 19 more were wounded.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian strikes on eastern Ukraine have killed at least six people overnight... Three more people were killed overnight and at least 19 others wounded in Russian attacks in the northern region of Sumy.

key_facts.fact: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned both Russia and Ukraine on Aug. 6 over rising civilian deaths, calling escalating strikes on populated areas a violation of international law that 'must stop immediately.'
key_facts.excerpt: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned both Russia and Ukraine on Thursday over rising civilian deaths, calling the escalating strikes on populated areas a violation of international law that "must stop immediately".

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said on Aug. 6 that the US-backed negotiation track is on pause and Kyiv is waiting for the American negotiating team to arrive, adding that only a Zelenskyy-Putin summit could give peace efforts real momentum.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Sybiha, only a top-level meeting between Zelenskyy and Putin can provide genuine momentum to peace efforts. However, the track involving American partners is currently on pause, and Ukraine is awaiting the arrival of the U.S. negotiating team.

stories.headline: Livestream shopping app Whatnot raises $545M at a $20B valuation, nearly doubling its price

key_facts.fact: Whatnot closed a $545 million Series G round valuing the livestream shopping platform at $20 billion, nearly double the $11.5 billion it commanded after its October 2025 raise.
key_facts.excerpt: Whatnot, the livestream shopping platform, has closed a $545 million Series G round, nearly doubling its worth from the $11.5 billion it commanded after its October 2025 raise.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed and Avra, with new investors Kleiner Perkins and Wellington Management and continued participation from Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global and CapitalG.
key_facts.excerpt: The round was led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed, and Avra, with new investors including Kleiner Perkins and Wellington Management, while existing shareholders such as Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, and CapitalG continued to participate.

key_facts.fact: The deal brings Whatnot's total funding to roughly $1.5 billion; the company was founded in 2019 and started out selling Funko Pop collectibles.
key_facts.excerpt: The company told Fortune exclusively about the round, which puts its total funding at roughly $1.5 billion across all stages.

key_facts.fact: Whatnot has expanded from collectibles into hundreds of categories including designer handbags and fresh groceries and has processed more than one billion orders.
key_facts.excerpt: expanded its offerings from collectibles to hundreds of categories including designer handbags and fresh groceries, and now serves multiple international markets with over one billion orders processed.

key_facts.fact: The raise stands out in a venture market where most large cheques are going to AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: In AI-obsessed Silicon Valley, live commerce platform Whatnot just notched a new funding round valuing it at $20 billion
